docs.title: Correlations of the systematics across eras
docs.text:
The properties are read from config/Run3_<era>/systematics.yaml in the same block that contains name. They work for systematics, weights, derived_systematics and qcd_scale (with overrides in the individual variations). The nuisance name is resolved by common/systematic_correlations.py.

# One nuisance common to all eras
isCorrelated: true
Eras_correlated: all

# One independent nuisance for each physical era (2022 and 2022EE included)
isCorrelated: false

# One nuisance common only to these sub-eras; the others stay independent
isCorrelated: true
Eras_correlated: [2022, 2022EE]

# Two independent groups, each correlated internally
isCorrelated: true
Eras_correlated: [[2022, 2022EE], [2023, 2023BPix]]

Configure the corresponding blocks consistently in the eras involved. Names with or without Run3_ are accepted, and YAML years as numbers or strings. With isCorrelated: false, Eras_correlated is ignored. With true and without Eras_correlated, all is assumed. If both fields are absent, the previous convention remains, determined by the {era} placeholder in the name. Empty groups, overlapping groups or groups with duplicates are rejected.

Example with name: CMS_example_{era}:

Configuration Era Nuisance name false 2022EE CMS_example_2022EE true, all any CMS_example true, [2022, 2022EE] 2022 or 2022EE CMS_example_2022_2022EE true, [2022, 2022EE] 2023 CMS_example_2023

If the name does not contain {era}, the necessary suffix is added. The names of the skim columns do not change: what changes is the name of the nuisance in the ROOT templates and therefore in the datacards. The builders that discover the Up/Down pairs from the histograms inherit these correlations automatically.

docs.text:

The sources that are independent across years are correlated between 2022/2022EE and between 2023/2023BPix. 2024, 2025 and 2026 each have a distinct nuisance. docs.title: Production, merge and plots
docs.text:
The DNN/all_variables campaigns use --jes regrouped by default, with 11 JES families produced separately. The families with the _year suffix are translated into the skim source of the current era: for example JESRegrouped_Absolute_year → JESRegrouped_Absolute_2022EE. --jes total selects the previous JES Total model. Keep the same option in submit/check/hadd/merge/plot. The plot refuses the double counting of Total and regrouped when both are present.

./hmumu hist dnn_vbf submit --mode both --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix --jes regrouped
# After the jobs:
./hmumu hist dnn_vbf finish --mode both --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix --jes regrouped
./hmumu hist dnn_vbf check --mode both --stage all --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix --jes regrouped

For a single component: --families JESRegrouped_Absolute_year --mode syst. For all_variables replace the campaign name; for a different JES model use a dedicated --output-dir.

The era merge builds templates with the total yield, varying only the eras affected by the nuisance. Example: nominals 10 and 20, variation +2 in the first era → combined nominal 30, varied template 32 (not 12). For inputs containing only variations, the direct command requires Central:

./hmumu merge-eras /production/PU_hadded \
  --nominal-dir /production/Central_hadded \
  --eras 2022,2022EE --output-era 2022_2022EE --run

The campaigns pass --nominal-dir automatically. Writes are atomic per file. The plots resolve the names from the same configuration, sum the correlated variations and combine the independent nuisances in quadrature.

After a change of the correlations, regenerate the affected templates (submit --force, or a new output directory), then hadd and merge. Only renaming the files or only redoing the plots does not apply the new policy. Old merges not completed with the nominals must be rebuilt; the campaign receipts have a new version and do not certify the old merges.

docs.text:
source env.sh
python3 -m pytest -q tests studies

The tests need the CMSSW environment (ROOT, correctionlib) but no EOS access. Some compile snippets of the C++ headers (corrections/jets.h, analysis/AnalysisTools.h) and run them on synthetic events, so they follow the production code.

docs.title: Changing the analysis
docs.text:
A variable: define the column in common/add_vars.py (or where its inputs are built), add its binning to config/plot/histograms.yaml, list it in variables of config/<era>/maincfg.yaml to have it in all_variables. ./hmumu where <column> shows where a column is defined, configured and used; ./hmumu vars <substring> lists the defined columns.

A selection, region or category: config/<era>/selections.yaml, one per era. Regions and categories with store: True are the ones campaigns produce with --regions all/--categories all.

A systematic: its variation in corrections/ or as a weight, its entry in config/<era>/systematics.yaml with the nuisance name and cross-era correlation (SYSTEMATIC_CORRELATIONS.md), and, if it is a new family, the family in SYSTEMATICS of the campaign configs.

A campaign: a new config/campaigns/<name>.sh (see the README); ./hmumu hist <name> paths checks it. A variant of an existing campaign can source it and override a few variables, as dnn_vbf_dy_unweighted.sh does.

Before merging a change to physics code, produce the same small histogram request with the old and the new code and compare them bin by bin:

python3 histograms/hist_maker.py --era Run3_2025 --dataset VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg \
    --input-manifest "$HMUMU_MANIFESTS/Run3_2025/VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg.json" \
    --output-file /tmp/$USER/new.root --systematics Central Muon \
    --variables DNN_NNOutput m_mumu --mass-regions Signal_Fit --categories VBF --max-files 4

Multithreaded RDataFrame sums in a different order at every run: expect relative differences of order 1e-15, identical entries.

docs.title: Using the analysis selection in your own code
docs.text:
common.prepare_rdf.prepare_rdf applies the variables, selections and weights of the analysis to a skim, for histograms, tuples or numpy arrays. Call it once per graph, before any action:

from common.utilities import initialize_root_runtime
from common.prepare_rdf import prepare_rdf

initialize_root_runtime()          # loads analysis/AnalysisTools.h; required when passing rdf=
nodes = prepare_rdf(
    rdf=raw_skim_rdf,              # or input_dir=/input_files=
    dataset_name=dataset_name, era=era, is_data=False,
    selections_cfg=sel_cfg, systematics_cfg=syst_cfg,
    seg_dict=dataset_seg_dict,     # normalisation of the WHOLE dataset, also for a subset of files
    enable_dy012j=True, enable_dyptll=True, enable_dynjets=True,
    split_jet_multiplicity=True,
    additional_cuts=None,          # e.g. the GenVBFFilter cut of the 105-160 DY halves
)
inclusive = nodes["inclusive"]

The result is an ordered dict: inclusive first, then the ggF 0J/1J/≥2J and VBF Hard/PU components (exclusive within their selection; the DY_inclusive_* views are sums of components, not to be added again). Data return only inclusive, empty inputs {}. enable_custom_weights=False drops the three DY reweights and keeps the nominal weights. The DY payloads come from the dataset's reweight_jsons in process_names.yaml unless given explicitly. prepare_region_dataframes builds the region/category/systematic views. additional_cuts from samples.yaml are not applied for you.

Training tuples from the skims: common/README.md.

Both networks are applied in the framework in the same way: - each event is scored by model FullEventId % 4, so never by a model that saw it in training; - the input standardisation is inside the ONNX graph; - the score is re-evaluated for every JES, JER and muon scale/resolution variation (dnn_application.ApplyDNNVariations, since 29 September 2026).

The production DNN was trained outside this repository (A. Yeagle, OGDNN_big_run). The VBF selector was trained here, in studies/vbf_selector/.

docs.title: Results to date
docs.text:
• H→μμ, DNN fit. Expected significance 2.10σ (toysFreq Asimov, SR + H sideband, 7 eras, DY lnn), 2.48 with statistics only. These numbers use the old dnn_vbf_weighted templates, whose jet and muon systematics are invalid, and have to be redone. Details: combine/RESULTS.md.
  • EWK Z normalisation. If it is left free, the expected significance drops from 2.14 to 1.63: this is the reason for the VBF selector (why).
  • VBF split CC/CF/FF. +1.8% (2.366 → 2.410), without shape systematics.
  • VBF selector.
  • AUC 0.90 in the Z sideband and 0.82 in the H sideband and SR; about 0.855 in 2022–23 and 0.815 in 2024–26, which follows the horn veto.
  • SHAP: it is a classifier of the tag-jet kinematics.
  • As a VBF category (counting): 1.105 against 1.014 for the cut-based category; the gain comes from the ggF side.
  • EWK Z in the sidebands. r = 1.051 ± 0.033 (DY Hard/PU, no shape systematics). This is not yet a measurement: the eras range from 0.62 to 1.27, the Z and H sidebands give 1.02 and 1.70, and the DY shape is mismodelled.

docs.title: From the DNN fits to an EWK Z fit with the VBF selector
docs.text: 2026-10-02. Why the H->mumu VBF fit needs a measured EWK Z normalisation, and why that measurement is done in the dimuon sidebands with the VBF selector. Every number below is an expected significance on the pre-fit Asimov (r = 1), 7 eras (2022-2026), DNN DNN_NNOutput in the VBF category, unless stated otherwise. Sources at the end.

docs.title: 1. The DNN fit, region by region
docs.text:
The signal fit uses the SR (Signal_Fit_VBF, 115-135 GeV) and optionally the H sideband (H_sideband_VBF, 110-115 and 135-150 GeV), with three ways of treating the DY jet components (Hard / one pile-up jet / two pile-up jets):

DY model SR only SR + H sideband SR only, DY scales shape-only SR + H sideband, DY scales shape-only lnn (Hard, PU1, PU2 constrained by the 012J fit) 2.00 2.13 2.07 2.17 rateparam-pu (PU free) 1.92 2.09 2.01 2.13 rateparam-both (PU and Hard free) 1.64 1.99 1.64 1.99 inclusive (one DY template, free) – 2.03 – –

Stat only (every constrained nuisance frozen): 2.51 for lnn. Three things are visible:

  • The H sideband helps exactly as much as the DY is left free: +6% with lnn, +9% with rateparam-pu, +21% with rateparam-both. It constrains the DY, which is the same process in SR and sideband.
  • Treating the DY QCD scales as shape-only (their normalisation already comes from the 012J fit in the Z sideband) is worth +2-4%.
  • The systematics cost ~15% (2.17 against 2.51). The freeze breakdown of the best card (SR + H sideband, shape-only, lnn) says where:
frozen significance nothing 2.17 theory (QCD scales, PDF, parton shower) 2.31 QCD scales of V processes (DY and EWK Z) 2.28 MC statistics 2.28 JES + JER 2.19 luminosity 2.19 DY normalisations, muons, pile-up 2.17 each

The largest single impact on r is QCD_fac_scale_V (±0.13), ahead of the MC statistics of the last DNN bins, JER and luminosity.

docs.title: 2. What the DNN fit assumes about EWK Z
docs.text:
In the three highest DNN bins of the SR, where the sensitivity is, the background is made of DY and EWK Z (pre-fit, lnn):

era EWK Z / background DY / background EWK Z / signal 2022 0.28 0.61 1.5 2022EE 0.29 0.58 1.6 2023 0.21 0.68 1.6 2023BPix 0.23 0.67 1.6 2024 0.22 0.69 1.6 2025 0.19 0.68 1.7 2026 0.36 0.54 1.5

EWK Z is a fifth to a third of the background and about 1.6 times the signal. Yet in every DNN card its normalisation is constrained only by the generator integration error of the cross section (±0.5%), plus the QCD-scale and parton-shower shapes. The fit treats the EWK Z yield as known.

How much that matters (SR + H sideband, lnn, high-score SR in the fit):

EWK Z normalisation significance change as in the cards (±0.5%) 2.14 – lnN 10% 2.07 −3% lnN 30% 1.86 −13% free (rateParam common to SR and H sideband) 1.63 −23%

So the sensitivity rests on a number that is not measured. Note the last row: the H sideband is in that fit, and still the DNN fit cannot tell EWK Z from DY on its own. The DNN separates H from background, not EWK Z from DY.

docs.title: 3. Why the EWK Z normalisation is not "known"
docs.text:
• The EWK Z prediction (madgraph, herwig/pythia showers, generated with m(jj) > 120 GeV at LHE) has never been checked on data in this phase space. The generator cut itself costs little (0.75% of the EWK Z yield in the VBF category sits at 120 < m(jj, LHE) < 150 GeV, with a <1% effect on the DNN shape: results/ewk_lhe_mjj/).
  • The pre-fit data/MC ratio in the sidebands follows the VBF-selector score, differently in each era (figure prefit_ratio_by_era): in the Z sideband it falls from 1.05 to ~0.90 in 2022 and 2022EE, stays flat in 2023 and 2023BPix, rises by ~5% in 2024 and by 10-20% in 2025 and 2026 (up to ~30% in the H sideband in 2026). The pre-fit band of these cards (lumi, cross sections, MC statistics, no shape systematics) is ~1%: something in DY or EWK Z is mismodelled exactly in the VBF-like topology where the DNN puts the signal, and it is not the same in every era.

docs.title: 4. The EWK Z fit with the VBF selector
docs.text:
The measurement goes where the Higgs is absent: the Z sideband and the H sideband, which share the VBF selection with the SR but not its m(mumu) window (H sideband in 2024: 0.6 VBF H + ggH events against 199 EWK Z). The variable is the VBF selector, a classifier trained to separate EWK Z from DY in that topology (studies/vbf_selector/), so that the fit can tell the two apart, which the DNN cannot. EWK Z is the signal of this fit (r = EWK Z yield / prediction); the DY gets free normalisations per channel, split in hard and pile-up jets (hard-pu), with the alternatives single (one DY template) and hard-pu-lnn (DY constrained by the 012J fit).

Results so far, without the shape systematics (luminosity, cross sections, free DY, MC statistics; combine/results_fit_matrix/SUMMARY.md):

DY model expected precision on r (all eras) r on data (all eras) r on data per era hard-pu ±0.032 (stat ±0.013) 1.05 ± 0.03 0.62-1.27 hard-pu-lnn ±0.030 1.12 ± 0.03 0.52-1.48 single ±0.031 0.80 ± 0.03 0.28-1.51
  • The precision is there: ±3% on the EWK Z normalisation would cost the DNN fit almost nothing (between the 2.14 of ±0.5% and the 2.07 of ±10%), while leaving it free costs 23%.
  • The eras do not agree (r from 0.5 in 2022 to 1.3-1.5 in 2024/2026, far beyond the errors), and the DY model matters: a single DY template cannot follow the data in 2025 and the fit runs away (r = 0.28 with the luminosity nuisance at its boundary), while the hard/pile-up split describes the same data within 1%. This is a statement about the modelling, and it is exactly what the DNN fit would inherit silently.

docs.title: 5. What comes next
docs.text:
1. EWK Z fit with every shape systematic (JES, JER, muon scale and resolution re-evaluate the selector score event by event): production of the shifted templates is being completed, then studies/vbf_selector/fit_ewkz_systematics.py and combine/run_fit_matrix.sh vbfsel. The question is whether the era spread is absorbed by the systematics or is a real mismodelling.
  2. Carry the measurement into the DNN fit: an EWK Z normalisation common to SR and H sideband, either constrained by the sideband result (lnN with its error) or fitted together with the Z and H sideband channels of the selector in one combined card.
  3. Fix what the DNN cards miss: no normalisation uncertainty at all on TT, ST, TW, VV, VVV, W, TTX, SingleH (their cross sections are not found in crossSections13p6TeV.yaml by process name); the VBF-selector fit already builds them per source.

docs.title: Guida al framework: da NanoAOD a combine
docs.text:
Aggiornata al 2026-10-06. Un'unica guida per tutta l'analisi, nell'ordine in cui si eseguono i passi: setup, skim, validazione, pesi DY, istogrammi, plot, datacard e fit, con una ricetta per ogni caso. Tutti i comandi si copiano così come sono, dalla radice del repository, dopo source env.sh.

La versione inglese è guide.md; le due hanno le stesse sezioni. I risultati non sono in questa guida: stanno in status.md (tutti gli studi), combine/RESULTS.md (fit DNN) e combine/results_fit_matrix/SUMMARY.md (matrice dei fit). Pagine di riferimento: correlazioni delle sistematiche, perché il fit EWK Z, metodo del reweighting DY, correzioni e payload, struttura del codice e test.

Template da usare (2026-10-06). I template dnn_vbf_weighted (hmumu hist dnn_vbf) non ricalcolano la DNN per JES, JER e scala/risoluzione dei muoni: le loro sistematiche di jet e muoni sono sbagliate, e così ogni fit DNN fatto con essi. Usare dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst con --eta-categories incl (sezione 7).

docs.title: 1. Panoramica
docs.text:
NanoAOD ──skim──> skim ──validate──> manifest ──dy-weights──> payload DY
        ──hist──> istogrammi ──hadd──> per processo ──merge-syst──> template (Hists_systMerged)
        ──plot──> Data/MC, shape delle sistematiche
        ──combine──> datacard ──fit_suite / run_fit_matrix──> r, significanza, pull, impact, scan, pre/post-fit

Una sola riga di comando, ./hmumu <stadio> <azione>, esegue ogni stadio; ogni comando stampa ciò che lancia, --dry-run mostra il piano senza fare nulla, --help funziona ovunque (./hmumu hist dnn_vbf --help).

stadio comando output (chiavi di config/paths.yaml) liste di file ./hmumu skim files config/<era>/samples_withfiles.yaml skim ./hmumu skim submit\|check $HMUMU_SKIM/<era>/<dataset>/skim_N.root manifest ./hmumu validate $HMUMU_MANIFESTS/<era>/<dataset>.json pesi DY ./hmumu dy-weights run reweights/dy_*_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/*.json istogrammi ./hmumu hist <campagna> submit\|hadd\|merge-syst $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/<campagna>/... controlli python3 tools/check_templates.py – plot ./hmumu hist <campagna> plot, ./hmumu plot, plot_systematics_campaign.py $HMUMU_WWW/... datacard ./hmumu combine cards, build_signal_extended_datacards.py, fit_ewkz_systematics.py combine/results_*/ fit ./hmumu combine fit, combine/fit_suite.py, combine/run_fit_matrix.sh combine/results_*/ tutto dopo gli skim ./hmumu chain all – cosa manca ./hmumu status –

L'analisi è la ricerca VBF H→μμ in Run 3, sette ere: 2022, 2022EE, 2023, 2023BPix, 2024, 2025, 2026. La variabile del fit è l'output della DNN VBF (DNN_NNOutput) nella categoria VBF. Regioni di massa (config/<era>/selections.yaml):

regione m(μμ) [GeV] fit plot Signal_Fit (SR) 115–135 sì, blindata sopra DNN 0.8 sì, blindata H_sideband 110–115, 135–150 sì sì Signal_ext 110–150 = Signal_Fit + H_sideband no (conterebbe due volte gli eventi) sì Z_sideband 70–110 regione di controllo, plot post-fit del fit ai dati sì mass_inclusive 60–150 no sì

I template con sistematiche servono in tutte le regioni: il fit legge solo i suoi canali, i plot mostrano le bande di sistematica pre-fit ovunque e il post-fit nelle regioni di controllo. Poiché il routing (6.5) riempie Signal_ext e mass_inclusive con i campioni DY/EWK inclusivi, Signal_ext con i campioni 105–160 si ottiene sommando Signal_Fit e H_sideband. Un secondo classificatore, il VBF selector (VBFSel_NNOutput), serve a misurare la normalizzazione dell'EWK Z (Z da VBF) nelle sideband.

docs.title: 2. Setup
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:valeriadamante/Hmumu_analysis.git
cd Hmumu_analysis
source env.sh                                    # bash o zsh
voms-proxy-init --voms cms --valid 192:00 --out data/voms.proxy
./hmumu doctor                                   # controlla il setup
./hmumu paths                                    # dove si legge e si scrive

env.sh:

  • crea un'area CMSSW in soft/ la prima volta (CMSSW_15_0_2; source env.sh --cmssw-version CMSSW_15_3_0 per un'altra) e la carica: ROOT, correctionlib, uproot, i pacchetti python;
  • imposta ANALYSIS_PATH e PYTHONPATH sul checkout e fa cd nel checkout (spostarsi altrove solo dopo il source);
  • definisce run_combine_tool, combine, combine_cards: combine v11 dal container su CVMFS, nessuna compilazione locale (COMBINE_IMAGE sceglie un'altra immagine);
  • esporta le posizioni di storage come HMUMU_<CHIAVE>.

Gli argomenti di uno script che lo carica vengono ignorati, quindi source env.sh si può usare dentro altri script. Il proxy grid serve agli skim (xrootd) e viene passato a ogni job Condor; X509_USER_PROXY, se definito, ha la precedenza su data/voms.proxy.

docs.title: Posizioni di storage
docs.text:
Ogni percorso fuori dal repository è una chiave di config/paths.yaml:

chiave contenuto skim skim, <skim>/<era>/<dataset>/skim_N.root + report_N.json skim_no_horn_veto skim 2025/2026 senza horn veto sui jet manifests manifest di validazione dy_weight_histograms input dei fit dei pesi DY (jet/, ptll/, njets/) histograms tutte le campagne di istogrammi sync area di scambio per la sincronizzazione www area web dei plot proxy proxy grid per i job Condor 
./hmumu paths skim                               # un solo valore
export HMUMU_SKIM=/eos/user/j/jdoe/skim_v4       # sovrascrive una chiave
export HMUMU_PATHS=~/hmumu_paths.yaml            # o un file con le sole chiavi da cambiare

Precedenza: HMUMU_<CHIAVE>, poi HMUMU_PATHS, poi config/paths.yaml. I valori possono riferirsi ad altre chiavi ("{eos_user}/manifests_skim_v4") e al checkout ("{repo}/data/voms.proxy"). Nel codice i percorsi si leggono con common.paths.path(chiave) (Python) o $HMUMU_<CHIAVE> (shell), mai scritti per esteso.

docs.title: Configurazione per era
docs.text:
Le ere non sono copie l'una dell'altra (il blocco categories: cambia tra 2022–2023 e 2024–2026): leggere sempre il file dell'era su cui si lavora.

file contenuto config/<era>/maincfg.yaml luminosità, golden JSON, correzioni, variabili degli istogrammi config/<era>/samples.yaml dataset, percorsi NanoAOD, additional_cuts config/<era>/samples_withfiles.yaml liste di file risolte (generato, non in git) config/<era>/process_names.yaml dataset → processi, payload dei pesi DY (reweight_jsons), split_jet_components config/<era>/selections.yaml oggetti, regioni di massa, categorie (store: True = prodotte da --regions all) config/<era>/systematics.yaml variazioni, nomi dei nuisance, correlazione tra ere config/<era>/skim_cfg.yaml processi da skimmare, chunking config/plot/histograms.yaml binning, blinding (blind_range) config/histogram_sample_routing.yaml quale campione DY/EWK riempie quale regione di massa config/crossSections13p6TeV.yaml sezioni d'urto e loro incertezze config/campaigns/*.sh campagne di istogrammi (sezione 6)

docs.title: 3. Skim
docs.text: Lo skim legge NanoAOD, applica selezione degli oggetti e correzioni (analysis/, corrections/) e salva gli oggetti corretti e le primitive nominali e variate. Le categorie si definiscono dopo, a livello di istogrammi, quindi si possono cambiare senza rifare gli skim finché le primitive sono salvate.

docs.title: 3.1 Liste di file
docs.text:
./hmumu skim files --era Run3_2024 --use-ext     # un'era per chiamata; --use-ext aggiunge le estensioni
# per passare prima a versioni NanoAOD più nuove:
python3 htcondor/update_nanoaod_versions.py --era Run3_2024,Run3_2025 --include-data --dry-run
python3 htcondor/update_nanoaod_versions.py --era Run3_2024,Run3_2025 --include-data --in-place
git diff config/Run3_*/samples.yaml

docs.title: 3.2 Sottomissione
docs.text:
./hmumu skim plan    --era 2024                     # i comandi del submitter
./hmumu skim dry-run --era 2024                     # chunk mancanti, nessuna sottomissione
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2024 --max-submit-jobs 1 # un job di prova
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2024                     # tutta l'era
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2025 --dataset VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig   # un dataset

Senza --era si selezionano tutte e sette le ere. Si sottomettono solo i chunk senza output, quindi submit riprende anche una produzione interrotta; per rifare un chunk cancellare skim_N.root e report_N.json.

opzione effetto --dataset NOME un dataset (ripetibile) --variant with\|without\|both 2025/2026: con/senza horn veto sui jet (default both) --n-events N prova, N eventi per job, in <skim>_testN --output PATH un'altra base per gli skim --max-submit-jobs N, --max-parallel-jobs N limitazione dei job HMUMU_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS (variabile d'ambiente, default 3000) tetto globale: job idle + running dell'utente, tutte le campagne; un cluster materializza al massimo questi job e viene sottomesso solo quando in coda c'è spazio --proxy PATH proxy da passare ai job

Chunk: al massimo 5 GB e 5 file per job (target_chunk_size_gb, max_files_per_chunk in skim_cfg.yaml); la mappa chunk → file e i log dei job stanno in htcondor/<nome skim>/<era>/<dataset>/.

docs.title: 3.3 Controllo
docs.text:
Un job ucciso dopo lo Snapshot lascia un .root completo senza report; un file troncato si apre ma ha meno eventi di quanti ne dichiara il report. skim check apre ogni chunk, legge l'ultimo evento e confronta con il report:

./hmumu skim check --era 2024 --output results/skim_v4/check_Run3_2024.json
./hmumu skim check --era 2025 --no-horn-veto
python3 analysis/check_duplicate_mc.py skim_0.root [skim_1.root]   # eventi duplicati

I dataset vuoti (nessun evento in nessun file) rompono gli strumenti che leggono direttamente gli skim; per elencarli:

cd "$HMUMU_SKIM" && for era in */; do for d in "$era"*/; do
  ls -l "$d"*.root 2>/dev/null | awk -v d="$d" '$5>10000{ok=1} END{if(!ok) print "EMPTY", d}'
done; done

docs.title: 4. Manifest di validazione
docs.text:
I job degli istogrammi leggono un manifest per dataset: le coppie valide skim_N.root/report_N.json e la normalizzazione dell'intero dataset (così un job su un sottoinsieme di file è comunque normalizzato correttamente).

./hmumu validate --eras 2024                    # tutti i dataset skimmati, su Condor
./hmumu validate --eras 2022,2022EE --dry-run
./hmumu validate --eras 2025 --no-horn-veto
./hmumu validate --eras 2024 --datasets signals,EWK --local

Si scrivono solo i manifest mancanti. Un dataset senza manifest viene escluso dalle campagne e segnalato come [UNAVAILABLE]: non lanciare istogrammi finché mancano manifest.

docs.title: 5. Pesi DY
docs.text:
Tre correzioni del DY ricavate dai dati, fittate nella Z sideband in un ordine fisso, ognuna sopra la precedente:

stadio campagna payload jet: normalizzazione delle componenti di jet (0J, 1J Hard/PU, 2J Hard/PU1/PU2, VBF Hard/PU) dy012j_skim_v4 reweights/dy_012j_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_012j_reweight.json ptll: shape di pT(μμ) per categoria di jet dy_ptll_skim_v4 reweights/dy_ptll_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_ptll_reweight_smart.json njets: molteplicità dei jet selezionati, ggF e VBF dy_njets_skim_v4 reweights/dy_njets_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_njets_reweight.json

I payload usati sono i reweight_jsons del processo DY in config/<era>/process_names.yaml, uno per era. Il metodo è descritto in sync/dy_reweighting.md.

./hmumu dy-weights run --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026

run fa un passo e ritorna: sottomette il primo stadio incompleto, oppure ne fa hadd e fit quando i suoi istogrammi ci sono. Exit code 3 = sottomesso, in attesa di Condor (non è un errore); 0 = tutti e tre i payload aggiornati. Richiamarlo dopo ogni ondata di job, oppure lasciare che ./hmumu chain dy-weights aspetti. Un payload più vecchio dei suoi istogrammi di input viene rifittato.

Passo per passo:

./hmumu dy-weights check         --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights submit        --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights hadd          --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights fit           --weight-stage jet --eras 2024 [--fit-option --pu1-pu2=tied]
./hmumu dy-weights check-weights --weight-stage jet --eras 2024

I fit scrivono i plot diagnostici accanto ai payload (dy_012j_{0J,1J,2J,VBF}_{pre,post}fit.png, {ggF_0J,...}_ptll_*.png, {ggF,VBF}_njets_*.png). Gli strumenti sono tools/derive_dy_012j_reweight.py, tools/derive_dy_ptll_njets_reweight.py, tools/derive_dy_njets_reweight.py.

Un refit invalida tutti gli istogrammi DY di quell'era: i controlli li marcano STALE e l'hadd si ferma. Vanno riprodotti:

./hmumu hist all_variables submit --mode central --eras 2025 --datasets region_auto --force

Le campagne applicano i tre pesi di default. Per scegliere: --dy-weights jet-component,ptll (due), --dy-weights '' (nessuno). Solo i dataset DY leggono i payload.

docs.title: 6. Istogrammi
docs.text:
histograms/hist_maker.py riempie gli istogrammi dagli skim di un dataset; una campagna lo esegue su Condor per ogni dataset, era e famiglia di sistematiche, poi aggrega. Motore: campaigns/workflow.py; ogni azione controlla input e output e si ferma (exit 1) se qualcosa è incompleto.

./hmumu hist <campagna> <azione> [opzioni]
./hmumu hist <campagna> paths          # input, output, ere, famiglie, opzioni risolte

docs.title: 6.1 Campagne
docs.text:
Un file per campagna in config/campaigns/ (CAMPAIGN_ROOT, ERAS, SYSTEMATICS, DATASETS, HIST_ARGS, dimensione dei job; vedi il README).

campagna contenuto sistematiche uso dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst DNN, VBF, Z/Signal_Fit/H sideband, incl/CC/CF/FF, componenti di jet DY/EWK tutte input del fit DNN dnn_vbf (radice dnn_vbf/ dal 2026-10-06) DNN, VBF, cinque regioni, componenti tutte plot DNN in tutte le regioni (anche Signal_ext, mass_inclusive) dnn_vbf_weighted (vecchia radice di dnn_vbf) lo stesso, prodotto il 2026-09-17 tutte, JES/JER/ScaRe sbagliate (sotto) da cancellare dnn_vbf_dy_unweighted come dnn_vbf senza pesi DY Central studio DNN all_variables ogni regione/categoria salvata × ogni variabile del maincfg tutte Data/MC vbf_eta_regions tutte le variabili, VBF diviso incl/CC/CF/FF Central studio η dnn_vbf_eta_regions DNN, VBF diviso incl/CC/CF/FF Central studio η vbf_selector_ewkz score del VBF selector e i suoi 24 input, Z e H sideband, componenti tutte input del fit EWK Z vbf_pair_definition coppie VBF alternative (VBF_PAIR_DEF=maxmjj\|hardest\|leading) Central studio della coppia dy012j_skim_v4, dy_ptll_skim_v4, dy_njets_skim_v4 input dei pesi DY Central via hmumu dy-weights jet_horn_veto Data/DY con e senza horn veto (costruita in workflow.py) Central studio horn veto

docs.title: 6.2 Azioni
docs.text: azione fa paths configurazione risolta check --stage S histograms, hadded, merged-eras, merged-syst, merged, all submit sottomette a Condor gli output mancanti e rotti local lo stesso, in locale validate manifest mancanti dei dataset della campagna hadd file per dataset → file per processo, per era e famiglia (--jobs N) merge-syst Central + tutte le famiglie → un file per processo (Hists_systMerged/), con ricevuta merge-era somma di ere in una pseudo-era (--merged-era NOME) plot plot per era; --merged per un'era unita finish hadd → merge-syst → plot (→ merge-era → plot uniti) opzione significato --eras 2024,2025 ere (default: ERAS della campagna) --mode central\|syst\|both Central, le famiglie, o entrambi --families PU,Muon sottoinsieme di famiglie --jes regrouped\|total 11 sorgenti JES raggruppate (default) o la totale --dy-weights ... pesi DY da applicare ('' nessuno) --regions, --categories, --variables, --datasets sovrascrivono la selezione --input-dir, --manifest-root, --output-dir sovrascrivono le basi --memory 20GB, --threads 8, --variable-batch-size N dimensione dei job --check-level files solo presenza/dimensione/data, senza aprire ROOT (veloce) --force rifà tutta la selezione --missing-only hadd: riprende, rimuovendo prima output vuoti/vecchi/illeggibili --dry-run stampa, non fa nulla

docs.title: 6.3 Produrre e validare una campagna (la sequenza standard)
docs.text:
source env.sh
C=dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst          # o vbf_selector_ewkz, all_variables, ...
E=2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026
./hmumu hist $C submit --mode both --eras $E
condor_q -af JobBatchName | sort | uniq -c                         # aspettare che sia vuoto
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage raw --quarantine
./hmumu hist $C submit --mode both --eras $E --check-level files   # rifà ciò che è in quarantena
./hmumu hist $C check --stage histograms --mode both --eras $E --check-level files
./hmumu hist $C hadd --mode both --eras $E
./hmumu hist $C merge-syst --mode both --eras $E
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage merged

Perché tools/check_templates.py: check --check-level files non vede un file troncato da un errore di scrittura su EOS, e --check-level root (uproot) può bloccarsi su di esso. Lo strumento apre ogni file con ROOT (zombie, "recovered", nessuna chiave) e, sui file uniti, controlla che la mediana di variazione/nominale di ogni template sia entro il 3% da 1 (un hadd che ha perso un dataset dà circa 0.5). --quarantine sposta i file grezzi rotti in <campagna>_quarantine_<data>/ (reversibile), così submit li riproduce. Dal 2026-10-06 hist_maker.py fa fallire un job con output troncato, così Condor lo ritenta.

Quando hadd/merge-syst protetti si rifiutano di partire per dataset che non si possono produrre (campioni FlashSim nelle campagne DNN: i loro skim non hanno SoftJetCleanedActivity_*; VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig senza manifest), lanciare direttamente i comandi pianificati:

./hmumu hist $C hadd --mode both --force --dry-run --check-level files 2>&1 \
  | grep hadd_hists_to_processes.py | sed 's/^\$ //' > hadd_cmds.sh
xargs -a hadd_cmds.sh -d '\n' -P 4 -I{} bash -c '{}'
./hmumu hist $C merge-syst --mode both --force --dry-run 2>&1 \
  | grep merge-systematics | sed 's/^\$ //' | while read -r c; do bash -c "$c --force"; done
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage merged

Il merge diretto non scrive la ricevuta (.workflow_syst_Run3_<era>.json): quando check_templates.py --stage merged dà OK, costruire le card con --allow-unmerged.

Job oltre le 8 ore (DY M-50 con tante variabili) vengono rimossi da Condor: mettere +JobFlavour = "tomorrow" in htcondor/<mode>/<dir>/submit.sub e risottometterlo, oppure condor_qedit <cluster> MaxRuntime 86400 mentre sono idle. Oppure dividere il dataset:

./hmumu shard submit --config all_variables --era 2024 --dataset DYto2Mu_M_50_amcatnloFXFX --shards 10
./hmumu shard merge  --config all_variables --era 2024 --dataset DYto2Mu_M_50_amcatnloFXFX --shards 10

Gli shard sono normalizzati con i report dell'intero dataset, quindi la somma coincide con l'output non diviso; merge rifiuta un insieme incompleto (--family, --cleanup).

docs.title: 6.4 Struttura degli output
docs.text:
<root>/<famiglia>/Run3_<era>/<dataset>.root                  per dataset (e per componente di jet)
<root>/<famiglia>_hadded/Run3_<era>/<processo>.root          per processo
<root>/Hists_systMerged/Run3_<era>/<processo>.root           Central + tutte le famiglie: input delle datacard
<root>/Central_hadded/<era unita>/...                        ere unite
<root>/.workflow_syst_Run3_<era>.json                        ricevuta del merge

Dentro un file: <regione di massa>_<categoria>/<variabile>, template variati <variabile>_<nuisance>Up/Down. Con --vbf-eta-regions un livello in più: Signal_Fit_VBF/{incl,CC,CF,FF}/DNN_NNOutput. Le componenti di jet sono file separati: <processo>_2J_Hard.root, _2J_PU1, _2J_PU2 (e 0J, 1J_Hard, 1J_PU).

docs.title: 6.5 Opzioni fisiche del produttore
docs.text:
• Routing dei campioni (config/histogram_sample_routing.yaml): in Signal_Fit e H_sideband DY ed EWK vengono dai campioni MLL 105–160, altrove da quelli inclusivi. Nel 2024–2026 il DY 105–160 è il campione inclusivo con GenVBFFilter==0 più quello filtrato VBF con GenVBFFilter==1 (additional_cuts di samples.yaml). Per questo Signal_ext non ha template DY/EWK e non si usa nel fit.
  • Componenti di jet (--pu-hard-jet-components): MC diviso secondo quanti dei due jet principali sono associati a un jet di generatore: 0J, 1J_Hard, 1J_PU, 2J_Hard, 2J_PU1, 2J_PU2. Processi divisi: split_jet_components di process_names.yaml.
  • Regioni η del VBF (--vbf-eta-regions): incl, CC (entrambi i jet VBF con |η| < 2.5), CF (uno), FF (nessuno). Si può combinare con le componenti di jet (corretto in hist_maker.py il 2026-10-06: prima dati e MC non diviso non ricevevano la divisione in η).
  • Famiglie di sistematiche: SYSTEMATICS della campagna; JES come 11 sorgenti raggruppate di default; nomi e correlazioni in config/<era>/systematics.yaml (SYSTEMATIC_CORRELATIONS.md). Le famiglie JES, JER e ScaRe riselezionano gli eventi e ricalcolano la DNN e il VBF selector (common/dnn_application.ApplyDNNVariations). Prima di questa correzione (dnn_vbf_weighted, 2026-09-17) la DNN era valutata una sola volta, sugli input nominali, e gli istogrammi variati usavano quello score nominale: una variazione poteva solo spostare eventi dentro o fuori dalla selezione, non lungo la DNN. Gli eventi selezionati solo con i jet variati hanno input nominali in cui la coppia VBF non esiste (variabili VBF al default -10000), quindi ricevevano uno score vicino a 0 e finivano tutti nel primo bin della DNN (JES Down, DY M-50 nella Z sideband: +56% nel bin 1, gli altri invariati), mentre la direzione opposta abbassava solo la normalizzazione.

docs.title: 6.6 Istogrammi singoli
docs.text:
./hmumu hist custom --era 2025 --dataset VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg \
    --variable DNN_NNOutput --region Signal_Fit --category VBF --one-file --run
./hmumu hist custom --era 2024 --datasets signals,EWK --systematics Central,Muon --condor --run

I canali si chiamano y<era>_<regione>[<cat η>], es. y2024_srlo, y2024_srhi, y2024_hsb, y2024_srCC.

Modelli DY

modello DY PU1 + PU2 DY Hard lnn lnN DYVBFZ_fit_2JPU1/2_<gruppo> lnN DYVBFZ_fit_2JHard_<gruppo> rateparam-pu un DY_norm_PU_<gruppo> libero lnN rateparam-both DY_norm_PU_<gruppo> DY_norm_Hard_<gruppo> inclusive un solo template DY (DYto2Mu_MLL105To160), un rateParam libero –

Gli lnN sono 1 + errore/valore delle componenti VBF del fit 012J (reweights/dy_012j_reweight_skim_v4/<gruppo>/dy_012j_reweight_fit.json), per gruppo 2022_2022EE, 2023_2023BPix, 2024, 2025, 2026. inclusive non accetta --dy-scale-shape-only.

Cosa c'è nella card

  • nuisance di shape da config/<era>/systematics.yaml (JES 11 sorgenti, JER 6 bin in η/pT, ID/iso/trigger dei muoni, scala/risoluzione dei muoni, PU, scale QCD, PDF, parton shower dell'EWK Z). Una colonna di shape è attiva solo dove entrambe le variazioni esistono, sono positive e non hanno bin negativi; il log della costruzione elenca quelle disattivate. CMS_scale_j_total_<era> è tolto (si usano le sorgenti raggruppate);
  • luminosità (datacard_inputs.lumidict; il 2026 usa i valori del 2025);
  • sezioni d'urto (7.3), lnN o rateParam del DY (sopra);
  • parton shower di EWK Z e VBF H (derived_systematics): herwig ± 0.5·|pythia − herwig|; il VBF H legge VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig dove esiste (2024–2026), e nel 2022–2023 riceve la differenza del 2024 riscalata per lumi(era)/lumi(2024) (CMS_hmm_VBFH_partonShower, un solo nuisance per tutte le ere);
  • autoMCStats (Barlow–Beeston lite);
  • un processo assente in un'era (es. SingleH) viene saltato.

docs.text: Le scrive studies/vbf_selector/fit_ewkz_systematics.py, che lancia anche i fit (sezione 8.6). Una card per fit: all, Z_sideband, H_sideband, <era>, <era>_Z, <era>_H, in combine/results_vbf_selector_ewkz_syst/<no_shape_systematics|systematics>/<modello DY>/datacard_<fit>.txt. docs.title: 7.3 Normalizzazioni dei processi uniti
docs.text:
Ogni fondo tranne il DY è una somma di dataset (TT = 3, ST = 6, TW = 6, VV = 10, VVV = 4, W = 3, TTX = 4, SingleH = 6, ...). --xsec-model per-source (default, condiviso con il VBF selector in combine/xsec_normalisation.py) dà a ogni processo un lnN per sorgente di sezione d'urto (xsec_TT, xsec_tW, xsec_ST_t, xsec_ST_s, xsec_WW, xsec_WZ, xsec_ZZ, xsec_ggH, xsec_qqH, ...):

kappa = 1 ± Σ_i f_i δ_i

con f_i la frazione di resa del dataset i nel canale (letta da <campagna>/Central/Run3_<era>/<dataset>.root) e δ_i la sua incertezza relativa in config/crossSections13p6TeV.yaml. La stessa sorgente è lo stesso nuisance in ogni processo ed era.

Perché non una colonna per dataset: per una normalizzazione (lnN) il kappa pesato è lo stesso vincolo, mentre spezzare i template dà decine di colonne a bassa statistica (ciascuna con autoMCStats, bin vuoti e i propri nuisance di shape) e un fit molto più lento. Colonne separate servono solo se un dataset ha bisogno di un trattamento di shape proprio.

Il log della costruzione (righe [XSEC]) elenca cosa manca nello yaml; va corretto lì, aggiungendo un alias in XSEC_ALIASES di combine/xsec_normalisation.py quando la chiave dello yaml è diversa dal nome del dataset. Lacune al 2026-10-06:

processo in crossSections13p6TeV.yaml W (WtoMuNu, WtoTauNu) nessuna incertezza VV, VVV, TTX solo l'errore di integrazione del generatore EWK Z solo errore di integrazione (±0.5%): da sostituire con la misura nelle sideband (ewkz_fit_motivation.md)

docs.text: Combine gira dal container: sempre tramite run_combine_tool (o gli script sotto, che lo usano).

docs.title: 8.1 Asimov pre-fit, Asimov toysFreq, dati
docs.text:
modo cos'è quando asimov -t -1 --expectSignal 1: rese attese con r = 1, nuisance al nominale sensibilità attesa del modello così come simulato toysfreq Asimov costruito dopo aver fittato i nuisance ai dati con r = 1 sensibilità attesa con il modello adattato ai dati data i dati osservati sideband; SR della DNN solo sotto 0.8 e solo background-only

Blinding. La SR della DNN sopra 0.8 non si guarda mai. Il --toysFreq in una riga fitta i nuisance a tutti i canali, SR sopra 0.8 inclusa, anche i parametri di statistica MC (il vecchio +7.7% di CC/CF/FF veniva da qui). Usare fit_suite.py --mode toysfreq --freq-mask '_srhi$' (due passi: un fit ai dati con la SR alta mascherata, poi l'Asimov da quello snapshot) oppure l'Asimov pre-fit (SE_SIG_OPTS=""). Fit ai dati della card DNN: background-only, SR alta mascherata (--mask '_srhi$' --data-bonly), oppure tutta la SR mascherata.

docs.text:
combine/run_signal_extended_fits.sh: costruisce la card e lancia significanza (totale e solo statistica), limiti, FitDiagnostics, impact e likelihood scan, per i modelli DY scelti.

  SE_BUILD_ARGS="--eta-categories incl --allow-unmerged" ./hmumu combine fit lnn
variabile default significato SE_ERAS tutte le ere con ricevuta ere SE_INPUT dnn_vbf_weighted/Hists_systMerged template (va impostato) SE_OUTPUT combine/results_signal_extended risultati, <output>/<modello>/ SE_STEPS build,significance,limits,fitdiagnostics,impacts,scan passi SE_BUILD_ARGS – opzioni del builder SE_ASIMOV -t -1 --expectSignal 1 vuoto = dati osservati (non con la SR) SE_SIG_OPTS --toysFreq "" = Asimov pre-fit (da usare con la SR) SE_RANGE --rMin -5 --rMax 10 intervallo di r SE_PARALLEL 8 fit di impact in parallelo SE_POINTS 60 punti dello scan SE_FITDIAG_OPTS --saveShapes --saveNormalizations opzioni di FitDiagnostics

Modelli: ./hmumu combine fit (senza argomento) = lnn, rateparam-pu, rateparam-both; inclusive va nominato. docs.text:
python3 combine/fit_suite.py --card combine/results_X/lnn/datacard.txt --name fit \
    --mode asimov toysfreq --freq-mask '_srhi$' --range=-5,10 \

Accanto alla card:

file contenuto results_<name>.json r, errori totale e solo statistico, significanza, per modo postfit_<name>_<mode>.root <canale>_prefit, <canale>_postfit con banda (da fit_shapes.py) pulls_<name>_<mode>.{txt,json} pull e constraint di ogni nuisance vincolato impacts_<name>_<mode>/impacts.{json,pdf} impact scan_<name>_<mode>/scan.{pdf,png} likelihood scan, totale e solo statistico

Una cartella per studio in studies/ con un README (domanda, metodo, comando, risultato); risultati riassunti in status.md.

Studi DNN, in dettaglio:

ERAS=2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2025; RES=$HMUMU_WWW/<tema>/studies
./hmumu study dnn binning     --eras $ERAS --results-dir $RES   # miglior taglio e ≤5 bin
./hmumu study dnn sensitivity --eras $ERAS --results-dir $RES   # significanza vs numero di bin
./hmumu study dnn performance --eras $ERAS --results-dir $RES   # pesato vs dnn_vbf_dy_unweighted
./hmumu study dnn roc --eras $ERAS --results-dir $RES --roc-max-files 30   # dagli skim
./hmumu study dnn studies     --eras $ERAS --results-dir $RES   # tutti e quattro
# la variante senza pesi, per "performance":
./hmumu study dnn submit-nondy --eras $ERAS; ./hmumu study dnn mirror-nondy --eras $ERAS
./hmumu study dnn submit-dy --eras $ERAS;    ./hmumu study dnn hadd --eras $ERAS

--roc-max-files serve in pratica (memoria: 23 GB senza, < 2 GB con 30); un'era alla volta, mai insieme ad altri lettori degli skim.

Un nuovo studio: studies/<nome>/ con README.md e un run.sh/run.py (così ./hmumu study <nome> lo trova) o il comando nel README; input tramite common.paths.path(...); output in results/ e $HMUMU_WWW.

docs.title: Framework guide: from NanoAOD to combine
docs.text:
Updated 2026-10-06. One guide for the whole analysis, in the order the steps are run: setup, skims, validation, DY weights, histograms, plots, datacards and fits, with one recipe per case. Every command can be copied as it is, from the repository root, after source env.sh.

The Italian version is guida.md; the two have the same sections. Results are not in this guide: they are in status.md (all the studies), combine/RESULTS.md (DNN fit) and combine/results_fit_matrix/SUMMARY.md (fit matrix). Reference pages: systematic correlations, why the EWK Z fit, DY reweighting method, corrections and payloads, code layout and tests.

Templates to use (2026-10-06). The dnn_vbf_weighted templates (hmumu hist dnn_vbf) do not re-evaluate the DNN for JES, JER and the muon scale/resolution: their jet and muon systematics are wrong, and so is every DNN fit made with them. Use dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst with --eta-categories incl (section 7).

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
NanoAOD ──skim──> skims ──validate──> manifests ──dy-weights──> DY payloads
        ──hist──> histograms ──hadd──> per process ──merge-syst──> templates (Hists_systMerged)
        ──plot──> Data/MC, systematic shapes
        ──combine──> datacards ──fit_suite / run_fit_matrix──> r, significance, pulls, impacts, scans, pre/post-fit

One command line, ./hmumu <stage> <action>, runs every stage; each prints what it runs, --dry-run shows the plan without doing anything, --help works everywhere (./hmumu hist dnn_vbf --help).

stage command output (keys of config/paths.yaml) file lists ./hmumu skim files config/<era>/samples_withfiles.yaml skims ./hmumu skim submit\|check $HMUMU_SKIM/<era>/<dataset>/skim_N.root manifests ./hmumu validate $HMUMU_MANIFESTS/<era>/<dataset>.json DY weights ./hmumu dy-weights run reweights/dy_*_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/*.json histograms ./hmumu hist <campaign> submit\|hadd\|merge-syst $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/<campaign>/... checks python3 tools/check_templates.py – plots ./hmumu hist <campaign> plot, ./hmumu plot, plot_systematics_campaign.py $HMUMU_WWW/... datacards ./hmumu combine cards, build_signal_extended_datacards.py, fit_ewkz_systematics.py combine/results_*/ fits ./hmumu combine fit, combine/fit_suite.py, combine/run_fit_matrix.sh combine/results_*/ everything after the skims ./hmumu chain all – what is missing ./hmumu status –

The analysis is the VBF H→μμ search in Run 3, seven eras: 2022, 2022EE, 2023, 2023BPix, 2024, 2025, 2026. The fit variable is the output of the VBF DNN (DNN_NNOutput) in the VBF category. Mass regions (config/<era>/selections.yaml):

region m(μμ) [GeV] fit plots Signal_Fit (SR) 115–135 yes, blinded above DNN 0.8 yes, blinded H_sideband 110–115, 135–150 yes yes Signal_ext 110–150 = Signal_Fit + H_sideband no (it would double count) yes Z_sideband 70–110 control region, post-fit plots of the data fit yes mass_inclusive 60–150 no yes

Templates with systematics are needed in every region: the fit reads only its channels, the plots show the pre-fit systematic bands everywhere and the post-fit in the control regions. Since the routing (6.5) fills Signal_ext and mass_inclusive with the inclusive DY/EWK samples, Signal_ext with the 105–160 samples is obtained by adding Signal_Fit and H_sideband. A second classifier, the VBF selector (VBFSel_NNOutput), is used to measure the EWK Z (VBF Z) normalisation in the sidebands.

docs.title: 2. Setup
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:valeriadamante/Hmumu_analysis.git
cd Hmumu_analysis
source env.sh                                    # bash or zsh
voms-proxy-init --voms cms --valid 192:00 --out data/voms.proxy
./hmumu doctor                                   # checks the setup
./hmumu paths                                    # where data are read and written

env.sh:

  • creates a CMSSW area in soft/ the first time (CMSSW_15_0_2; source env.sh --cmssw-version CMSSW_15_3_0 for another one) and loads it: ROOT, correctionlib, uproot, the python packages;
  • sets ANALYSIS_PATH and PYTHONPATH to the checkout and changes directory into it (cd elsewhere only after sourcing);
  • defines run_combine_tool, combine, combine_cards: combine v11 from the CVMFS container, no local build (COMBINE_IMAGE selects another image);
  • exports the storage locations as HMUMU_<KEY>.

Arguments of a script that sources it are ignored, so source env.sh is safe inside other scripts. The grid proxy is needed for the skims (xrootd) and is forwarded to every Condor job; X509_USER_PROXY, when set, wins over data/voms.proxy.

docs.title: Storage locations
docs.text:
Every path outside the repository is a key of config/paths.yaml:

key content skim skims, <skim>/<era>/<dataset>/skim_N.root + report_N.json skim_no_horn_veto 2025/2026 skims without the jet horn veto manifests validation manifests dy_weight_histograms inputs of the DY-weight fits (jet/, ptll/, njets/) histograms every histogram campaign sync synchronisation exchange area www web area of the plots proxy grid proxy for the Condor jobs 
./hmumu paths skim                               # one value
export HMUMU_SKIM=/eos/user/j/jdoe/skim_v4       # override one key
export HMUMU_PATHS=~/hmumu_paths.yaml            # or a file with only the keys you change

Precedence: HMUMU_<KEY>, then HMUMU_PATHS, then config/paths.yaml. Values can refer to other keys ("{eos_user}/manifests_skim_v4") and to the checkout ("{repo}/data/voms.proxy"). In code, paths are read with common.paths.path(key) (Python) or $HMUMU_<KEY> (shell), never written out.

docs.title: Per-era configuration
docs.text:
Eras are not copies of each other (the categories: block differs between 2022–2023 and 2024–2026): always read the file of the era you work on.

file content config/<era>/maincfg.yaml luminosity, golden JSON, corrections, histogram variables config/<era>/samples.yaml datasets, NanoAOD paths, additional_cuts config/<era>/samples_withfiles.yaml resolved file lists (generated, not in git) config/<era>/process_names.yaml datasets → processes, DY-weight payloads (reweight_jsons), split_jet_components config/<era>/selections.yaml objects, mass regions, categories (store: True = produced by --regions all) config/<era>/systematics.yaml variations, nuisance names, cross-era correlation config/<era>/skim_cfg.yaml processes to skim, chunking config/plot/histograms.yaml binning, blinding (blind_range) config/histogram_sample_routing.yaml which DY/EWK sample fills which mass region config/crossSections13p6TeV.yaml cross sections and their uncertainties config/campaigns/*.sh histogram campaigns (section 6)

docs.title: 3. Skims
docs.text: The skim reads NanoAOD, applies object selection and corrections (analysis/, corrections/) and stores corrected objects and the nominal and shifted primitives. Categories are defined later, at histogram level, so they can change without re-skimming as long as the primitives are stored.

docs.title: 3.1 File lists
docs.text:
./hmumu skim files --era Run3_2024 --use-ext     # one era per call; --use-ext adds the extensions
# moving to newer NanoAOD versions first:
python3 htcondor/update_nanoaod_versions.py --era Run3_2024,Run3_2025 --include-data --dry-run
python3 htcondor/update_nanoaod_versions.py --era Run3_2024,Run3_2025 --include-data --in-place
git diff config/Run3_*/samples.yaml

docs.title: 3.2 Submit
docs.text:
./hmumu skim plan    --era 2024                     # the submitter commands
./hmumu skim dry-run --era 2024                     # missing chunks, nothing submitted
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2024 --max-submit-jobs 1 # one test job
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2024                     # the whole era
./hmumu skim submit  --era 2025 --dataset VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig   # one dataset

Without --era all seven eras are selected. Only chunks without output are submitted, so submit also resumes; to redo a chunk delete its skim_N.root and report_N.json.

option effect --dataset NAME one dataset (repeatable) --variant with\|without\|both 2025/2026: with/without the jet horn veto (default both) --n-events N test, N events per job, to <skim>_testN --output PATH another skim base --max-submit-jobs N, --max-parallel-jobs N throttling HMUMU_MAX_QUEUED_JOBS (env, default 3000) global cap: idle + running jobs of the user, all campaigns; a cluster materialises at most this many jobs and is submitted only when the queue has room --proxy PATH proxy to forward

Chunks: at most 5 GB and 5 files per job (target_chunk_size_gb, max_files_per_chunk in skim_cfg.yaml); the chunk → files map and the job logs are in htcondor/<skim name>/<era>/<dataset>/.

docs.title: 3.3 Check
docs.text:
A job killed after the Snapshot leaves a full .root without its report; a truncated file opens but has fewer events than its report. skim check opens every chunk, reads the last event and compares with the report:

./hmumu skim check --era 2024 --output results/skim_v4/check_Run3_2024.json
./hmumu skim check --era 2025 --no-horn-veto
python3 analysis/check_duplicate_mc.py skim_0.root [skim_1.root]   # duplicated events

Empty datasets (no events in any file) break tools that read the skims directly; to list them:

cd "$HMUMU_SKIM" && for era in */; do for d in "$era"*/; do
  ls -l "$d"*.root 2>/dev/null | awk -v d="$d" '$5>10000{ok=1} END{if(!ok) print "EMPTY", d}'
done; done

docs.title: 4. Validation manifests
docs.text:
Histogram jobs read one manifest per dataset: the valid skim_N.root/report_N.json pairs and the normalisation of the whole dataset (so a job on a subset of files is still normalised correctly).

./hmumu validate --eras 2024                    # every skimmed dataset, on Condor
./hmumu validate --eras 2022,2022EE --dry-run
./hmumu validate --eras 2025 --no-horn-veto
./hmumu validate --eras 2024 --datasets signals,EWK --local

Only missing manifests are written. A dataset without a manifest is excluded by the campaigns and reported as [UNAVAILABLE]: do not start histograms while manifests are missing.

docs.title: 5. DY weights
docs.text:
Three data-driven DY corrections, fitted in the Z sideband in a fixed order, each on top of the previous one:

stage campaign payload jet: normalisation of the jet components (0J, 1J Hard/PU, 2J Hard/PU1/PU2, VBF Hard/PU) dy012j_skim_v4 reweights/dy_012j_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_012j_reweight.json ptll: pT(μμ) shape per jet category dy_ptll_skim_v4 reweights/dy_ptll_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_ptll_reweight_smart.json njets: selected-jet multiplicity, ggF and VBF dy_njets_skim_v4 reweights/dy_njets_reweight_skim_v4/<era>/dy_njets_reweight.json

The payloads used are the reweight_jsons of the DY process in config/<era>/process_names.yaml, one per era. The method is in sync/dy_reweighting.md.

./hmumu dy-weights run --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026

run does one step and returns: it submits the first incomplete stage, or hadds and fits it when its histograms are there. Exit code 3 = submitted, waiting for Condor (not an error); 0 = all three payloads up to date. Call it again after each wave, or let ./hmumu chain dy-weights wait. A payload older than its input histograms is refitted.

Step by step:

./hmumu dy-weights check         --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights submit        --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights hadd          --weight-stage jet --eras 2024
./hmumu dy-weights fit           --weight-stage jet --eras 2024 [--fit-option --pu1-pu2=tied]
./hmumu dy-weights check-weights --weight-stage jet --eras 2024

The fits write their diagnostic plots next to the payloads (dy_012j_{0J,1J,2J,VBF}_{pre,post}fit.png, {ggF_0J,...}_ptll_*.png, {ggF,VBF}_njets_*.png). The tools are tools/derive_dy_012j_reweight.py, tools/derive_dy_ptll_njets_reweight.py, tools/derive_dy_njets_reweight.py.

A refit invalidates every DY histogram of that era: the checks mark them STALE and hadd stops. Reproduce them:

./hmumu hist all_variables submit --mode central --eras 2025 --datasets region_auto --force

Campaigns apply the three weights by default. To choose: --dy-weights jet-component,ptll (two of them), --dy-weights '' (none). Only DY datasets read the payloads.

docs.title: 6. Histograms
docs.text:
histograms/hist_maker.py fills histograms from the skims of one dataset; a campaign runs it on Condor for every dataset, era and systematic family, then aggregates. Engine: campaigns/workflow.py; every action checks its inputs and outputs and stops (exit 1) on anything incomplete.

./hmumu hist <campaign> <action> [options]
./hmumu hist <campaign> paths          # resolved inputs, output, eras, families, options

docs.title: 6.1 Campaigns
docs.text:
One file per campaign in config/campaigns/ (CAMPAIGN_ROOT, ERAS, SYSTEMATICS, DATASETS, HIST_ARGS, job size; see the README).

campaign content systematics use dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst DNN, VBF, Z/Signal_Fit/H sideband, incl/CC/CF/FF, DY/EWK jet components all DNN fit input dnn_vbf (root dnn_vbf/ since 2026-10-06) DNN, VBF, five regions, components all DNN plots in every region (Signal_ext, mass_inclusive too) dnn_vbf_weighted (old root of dnn_vbf) the same, produced 2026-09-17 all, JES/JER/ScaRe wrong (below) to be deleted dnn_vbf_dy_unweighted as dnn_vbf without DY weights Central DNN study all_variables every stored region/category × every maincfg variable all Data/MC vbf_eta_regions all variables, VBF split incl/CC/CF/FF Central η study dnn_vbf_eta_regions DNN, VBF split incl/CC/CF/FF Central η study vbf_selector_ewkz VBF-selector score and its 24 inputs, Z and H sidebands, components all EWK Z fit input vbf_pair_definition alternative VBF pairs (VBF_PAIR_DEF=maxmjj\|hardest\|leading) Central pair study dy012j_skim_v4, dy_ptll_skim_v4, dy_njets_skim_v4 DY-weight inputs Central via hmumu dy-weights jet_horn_veto Data/DY with and without the horn veto (built in workflow.py) Central horn-veto study

docs.title: 6.2 Actions
docs.text: action does paths resolved configuration check --stage S histograms, hadded, merged-eras, merged-syst, merged, all submit submit missing and broken outputs to Condor local the same, here validate missing manifests of the campaign's datasets hadd dataset files → process files, per era and family (--jobs N) merge-syst Central + every family → one file per process (Hists_systMerged/), with a receipt merge-era sum of eras into a pseudo-era (--merged-era NAME) plot plots per era; --merged for a merged era finish hadd → merge-syst → plot (→ merge-era → merged plots) option meaning --eras 2024,2025 eras (default: the campaign's ERAS) --mode central\|syst\|both Central, the families, or both --families PU,Muon subset of families --jes regrouped\|total 11 regrouped JES sources (default) or the total --dy-weights ... docs.title: 6.3 Produce and validate a campaign (the standard sequence)
docs.text:
source env.sh
C=dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst          # or vbf_selector_ewkz, all_variables, ...
E=2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026
./hmumu hist $C submit --mode both --eras $E
condor_q -af JobBatchName | sort | uniq -c                         # wait until empty
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage raw --quarantine
./hmumu hist $C submit --mode both --eras $E --check-level files   # redo what was quarantined
./hmumu hist $C check --stage histograms --mode both --eras $E --check-level files
./hmumu hist $C hadd --mode both --eras $E
./hmumu hist $C merge-syst --mode both --eras $E
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage merged

Why tools/check_templates.py: check --check-level files does not see a file truncated by an EOS write error, and --check-level root (uproot) can hang on it. The tool opens every file with ROOT (zombie, "recovered", no keys) and, on the merged files, checks that the median of variation/nominal of each template is within 3% of 1 (a hadd that lost a dataset gives about 0.5). --quarantine moves the broken raw files to <campaign>_quarantine_<date>/ (reversible) so submit produces them again. Since 2026-10-06 hist_maker.py fails a job with a truncated output, so Condor retries it.

When the guarded hadd/merge-syst refuse to run because of datasets that cannot be produced (FlashSim samples in DNN campaigns: their skims lack SoftJetCleanedActivity_*; VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig without manifest), run the planned commands directly:

./hmumu hist $C hadd --mode both --force --dry-run --check-level files 2>&1 \
  | grep hadd_hists_to_processes.py | sed 's/^\$ //' > hadd_cmds.sh
xargs -a hadd_cmds.sh -d '\n' -P 4 -I{} bash -c '{}'
./hmumu hist $C merge-syst --mode both --force --dry-run 2>&1 \
  | grep merge-systematics | sed 's/^\$ //' | while read -r c; do bash -c "$c --force"; done
python3 tools/check_templates.py $HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/$C --stage merged

The direct merge writes no receipt (.workflow_syst_Run3_<era>.json): once check_templates.py --stage merged says OK, build the cards with --allow-unmerged.

Jobs longer than 8 h (DY M-50 with many variables) are removed by Condor: set +JobFlavour = "tomorrow" in htcondor/<mode>/<dir>/submit.sub and resubmit it, or condor_qedit <cluster> MaxRuntime 86400 while idle. Or shard the dataset:

./hmumu shard submit --config all_variables --era 2024 --dataset DYto2Mu_M_50_amcatnloFXFX --shards 10
./hmumu shard merge  --config all_variables --era 2024 --dataset DYto2Mu_M_50_amcatnloFXFX --shards 10

The shards are normalised with the dataset-wide reports, so their sum equals the unsharded output; merge refuses an incomplete set (--family, --cleanup).

docs.title: 6.4 Output layout
docs.text:
<root>/<family>/Run3_<era>/<dataset>.root                    per dataset (and per jet component)
<root>/<family>_hadded/Run3_<era>/<process>.root             per process
<root>/Hists_systMerged/Run3_<era>/<process>.root            Central + every family: the datacard input
<root>/Central_hadded/<merged era>/...                       merged eras
<root>/.workflow_syst_Run3_<era>.json                        merge receipt

Inside a file: <mass region>_<category>/<variable>, shifted templates <variable>_<nuisance>Up/Down. With --vbf-eta-regions one more level: Signal_Fit_VBF/{incl,CC,CF,FF}/DNN_NNOutput. Jet components are separate files: <process>_2J_Hard.root, _2J_PU1, _2J_PU2 (and 0J, 1J_Hard, 1J_PU).

docs.title: 6.5 Physics options of the producer
docs.text:
• Sample routing (config/histogram_sample_routing.yaml): in Signal_Fit and H_sideband DY and EWK come from the MLL 105–160 samples, elsewhere from the inclusive ones. In 2024–2026 the 105–160 DY is the inclusive sample with GenVBFFilter==0 plus the VBF-filtered one with GenVBFFilter==1 (additional_cuts of samples.yaml). Signal_ext therefore has no DY/EWK templates and is not used in the fit.
  • Jet components (--pu-hard-jet-components): MC split by how many of the two leading jets are matched to a generator jet: 0J, 1J_Hard, 1J_PU, 2J_Hard, 2J_PU1, 2J_PU2. Processes split: split_jet_components of process_names.yaml.
  • VBF η regions (--vbf-eta-regions): incl, CC (both VBF jets |η| < 2.5), CF (one), FF (none). Can be combined with the jet components (fixed in hist_maker.py on 2026-10-06: before, data and non-split MC got no η split).
  • Systematic families: SYSTEMATICS of the campaign; JES as 11 regrouped sources by default; names and correlations in config/<era>/systematics.yaml (SYSTEMATIC_CORRELATIONS.md). The JES, JER and ScaRe families re-select the events and re-evaluate the DNN and the VBF selector (common/dnn_application.ApplyDNNVariations). Before that fix (dnn_vbf_weighted, 2026-09-17) the DNN was evaluated once, on the nominal inputs, and the shifted histograms used that nominal score: a variation could only move events across the selection, not along the DNN. Events selected only with the shifted jets carry nominal inputs in which the VBF pair does not exist (VBF variables at the default -10000), so they got a score near 0 and piled up in the first DNN bin (JES Down, DY M-50 in the Z sideband: +56% in bin 1, other bins unchanged), while the opposite direction only lowered the normalisation.

docs.title: 7.1 DNN card (H→μμ)
docs.text:
IN=$HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst/Hists_systMerged
python3 combine/build_signal_extended_datacards.py --input $IN --allow-unmerged \
    --eras 2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026 \
    --eta-categories incl --dy-model lnn --channels sr,hsb --blind-split 0.8 \
    --output combine/results_X/lnn/datacard.txt
# the same through the CLI:
./hmumu combine cards --input $IN --allow-unmerged --eras 2024 --eta-categories incl \
    --dy-model lnn --output combine/results_X/lnn/datacard.txt
option values --input Hists_systMerged of the campaign (default: dnn_vbf_weighted, change it) --eras default every era with a merge receipt --channels sr (Signal_Fit_VBF), hsb (H_sideband_VBF), zsb (Z_sideband_VBF); e.g. sr,hsb --eta-categories incl (whole VBF) or CC,CF,FF (one channel and one DY normalisation per category) --dy-model lnn, rateparam-pu, rateparam-both, inclusive (below) --blind-split 0.8 SR split at DNN 0.8 into ..srlo/..srhi, so a data fit can mask the high part --dy-scale-shape-only DY QCD scales shape-only + QCD_{fac,ren}_scale_V_DYextrap lnN for the Z-sideband → channel extrapolation (templates in patched_templates/) --rateparam-scope group\|all one DY rateParam per era group or one for all eras --rate-param-range 0.2,5 rateParam range --xsec-model per-source\|per-process cross-section lnN (7.3); default per-source --variable default DNN_NNOutput --allow-unmerged accept eras without merge receipt (only after check_templates --stage merged OK)

Channels are named y<era>_<region>[<eta cat>], e.g. y2024_srlo, y2024_srhi, y2024_hsb, y2024_srCC.

DY models

model DY PU1 + PU2 DY Hard lnn DYVBFZ_fit_2JPU1/2_<group> lnN DYVBFZ_fit_2JHard_<group> lnN rateparam-pu one free DY_norm_PU_<group> lnN rateparam-both DY_norm_PU_<group> DY_norm_Hard_<group> inclusive one DY template (DYto2Mu_MLL105To160), one free rateParam –

The lnN are 1 + error/value of the VBF components of the 012J fit (reweights/dy_012j_reweight_skim_v4/<group>/dy_012j_reweight_fit.json), per group 2022_2022EE, 2023_2023BPix, 2024, 2025, 2026. inclusive cannot take --dy-scale-shape-only.

What is in the card

  • shape nuisances from config/<era>/systematics.yaml (JES 11 sources, JER 6 η/pT bins, muon ID/iso/trigger, muon scale/resolution, PU, QCD scales, PDF, EWK Z parton shower). A shape column is enabled only where both variations exist, are positive and have no negative bin; the build log lists the disabled ones. CMS_scale_j_total_<era> is dropped (the regrouped sources are used);
  • luminosity (datacard_inputs.lumidict; 2026 uses the 2025 values);
  • cross sections (7.3), DY lnN or rateParams (above);
  • parton shower of EWK Z and VBF H (derived_systematics): herwig ± 0.5·|pythia − herwig|; VBF H reads VBFHto2Mu_M125_powheg_herwig where it exists (2024–2026), and in 2022–2023 gets the 2024 difference scaled by lumi(era)/lumi(2024) (CMS_hmm_VBFH_partonShower, one nuisance for all eras);
  • autoMCStats (Barlow–Beeston lite);
  • a process absent in an era (e.g. SingleH) is skipped.

docs.title: 7.2 VBF-selector cards (EWK Z in the sidebands)
docs.text: Written by studies/vbf_selector/fit_ewkz_systematics.py, which also runs the fits (section 8.6). One card per fit: all, Z_sideband, H_sideband, <era>, <era>_Z, <era>_H, in combine/results_vbf_selector_ewkz_syst/<no_shape_systematics|systematics>/<dy model>/datacard_<fit>.txt. DY models: single (one DY template, free per channel), hard-pu (DY Hard and DY PU free per channel), hard-pu-lnn (constrained by the 012J fit); run_fit_ewkz_pu_split.py adds hard-pu1-pu2 (diagnostic). POI: the EWK Z signal strength.

docs.title: 7.3 Normalisations of the merged processes
docs.text:
Every background except DY is a sum of datasets (TT = 3, ST = 6, TW = 6, VV = 10, VVV = 4, W = 3, TTX = 4, SingleH = 6, ...). --xsec-model per-source (default, shared with the VBF selector in combine/xsec_normalisation.py) gives each process one lnN per cross-section source (xsec_TT, xsec_tW, xsec_ST_t, xsec_ST_s, xsec_WW, xsec_WZ, xsec_ZZ, xsec_ggH, xsec_qqH, ...):

kappa = 1 ± Σ_i f_i δ_i

with f_i the yield fraction of dataset i in the channel (read from <campaign>/Central/Run3_<era>/<dataset>.root) and δ_i its relative uncertainty in config/crossSections13p6TeV.yaml. The same source is the same nuisance in every process and era.

Why not one column per dataset: for a normalisation (lnN) the weighted kappa is the same constraint, while splitting the templates gives tens of low-statistics columns (each with autoMCStats, empty bins and its own shape nuisances) and a much slower fit. Separate columns are worth it only if a dataset needs its own shape treatment.

The build log ([XSEC] lines) lists what is missing in the yaml; fix it there, and add an alias in XSEC_ALIASES of combine/xsec_normalisation.py when the yaml key differs from the dataset name. Gaps on 2026-10-06:

process in crossSections13p6TeV.yaml W (WtoMuNu, WtoTauNu) no uncertainty VV, VVV, TTX generator integration error only EWK Z integration error only (±0.5%): to be replaced by the sideband measurement (ewkz_fit_motivation.md)

docs.title: 8. Fits
docs.text: Combine runs from the container: always through run_combine_tool (or the scripts below, which use it).

docs.title: 8.1 Pre-fit Asimov, toysFreq Asimov, data
docs.text:
mode what when asimov -t -1 --expectSignal 1: expected yields with r = 1, nuisances at nominal expected sensitivity of the model as simulated toysfreq Asimov built after fitting the nuisances to the data with r = 1 expected sensitivity once the model is adjusted to the data data the observed data sidebands; DNN SR only below 0.8 and only background-only

Blinding. The DNN SR above 0.8 is never looked at. The one-line --toysFreq fits the nuisances to every channel, SR above 0.8 included, MC-statistics parameters too (the old +7.7% of CC/CF/FF came from that). Use fit_suite.py --mode toysfreq --freq-mask '_srhi$' (two steps: a data fit with the high SR masked, then the Asimov from that snapshot) or the pre-fit Asimov (SE_SIG_OPTS=""). Data fits of the DNN card: background-only, high SR masked (--mask '_srhi$' --data-bonly), or the whole SR masked.

docs.title: 8.2 Significance, limits, impacts, scan: ./hmumu combine fit
docs.text:
combine/run_signal_extended_fits.sh: builds the card and runs significance (total and stat only), limits, FitDiagnostics, impacts, likelihood scan, for the chosen DY models.

IN=$HMUMU_HISTOGRAMS/dnn_vbf_eta_regions_syst/Hists_systMerged
E=2022,2022EE,2023,2023BPix,2024,2025,2026
SE_ERAS=$E SE_INPUT=$IN SE_OUTPUT=$PWD/combine/results_7eras_v2/base SE_SIG_OPTS="" \
  SE_BUILD_ARGS="--eta-categories incl --allow-unmerged" ./hmumu combine fit lnn
variable default meaning SE_ERAS every era with a receipt eras SE_INPUT dnn_vbf_weighted/Hists_systMerged templates (set it) SE_OUTPUT combine/results_signal_extended results, <output>/<model>/ SE_STEPS build,significance,limits,fitdiagnostics,impacts,scan steps SE_BUILD_ARGS – builder options SE_ASIMOV -t -1 --expectSignal 1 empty = observed data (not with the SR) SE_SIG_OPTS --toysFreq "" = pre-fit Asimov (use this with the SR) SE_RANGE --rMin -5 --rMax 10 r range SE_PARALLEL 8 parallel impact fits SE_POINTS 60 scan points SE_FITDIAG_OPTS --saveShapes --saveNormalizations FitDiagnostics options

Models: ./hmumu combine fit (no argument) = lnn, rateparam-pu, rateparam-both; inclusive must be named. Outputs in <SE_OUTPUT>/<model>/: card and workspace, significance/, limits/, fitdiagnostics/, impacts/ (JSON, PDF), scan/. To read the significance: grep -h "^Significance" <SE_OUTPUT>/*/significance/*.log.

docs.title: 8.3 Every test on one card: combine/fit_suite.py
docs.text:
python3 combine/fit_suite.py --card combine/results_X/lnn/datacard.txt --name fit \
    --mode asimov toysfreq --freq-mask '_srhi$' --range=-5,10 \
    --pulls --impacts --scan --scan-range=-1,3
option meaning --mode asimov toysfreq data one or more (8.1) --freq-mask REGEX channels left out of the data fit of toysfreq --mask REGEX channels masked in the data fit --data-bonly data: r = 0, no r reported --range=-5,10 r range --pulls, --impacts, --scan the tests --impacts-parallel 8, --scan-points 40, --scan-range=-1,3 their settings --no-stat-only, --redo-stat skip / redo the stat-only fits --samples N samples of the uncertainty band

Next to the card:

file content results_<name>.json r, total and stat-only errors, significance, per mode postfit_<name>_<mode>.root <channel>_prefit, <channel>_postfit with band (from fit_shapes.py) pulls_<name>_<mode>.{txt,json} pull and constraint of every constrained nuisance impacts_<name>_<mode>/impacts.{json,pdf} impacts scan_<name>_<mode>/scan.{pdf,png} likelihood scan, total and stat only

Stat-only fits freeze every constrained nuisance, run without --robustFit and with rMin = 0 (negative r gives negative yields). Pre/post-fit shapes come from combine/fit_shapes.py (bin-by-bin evaluation of the workspace, band by sampling), not from FitDiagnostics --saveWithUncertainties or PostFitShapesFromWorkspace, which take hours (19 h on 7 eras).
